title: Kelani Valley railway line ticket system out of service
byline: Due to a sudden outage in the newly introduced train ticketing system on the Kelani Valley railway line, tickets will not be issued to passengers travelling on morning train services today, the Railways Department said.

title: Apple unveils Siri AI makeover as Tim Cook bids farewell
byline: Apple has announced a significant overhaul of its digital assistant, unveiling Siri AI, which the company promised would offer a better artificial intelligence experience for users.

title: Mother wins three-decade legal battle over property against son
byline: A mother has emerged victorious in a 30-year legal battle against her son over a residential property after the Supreme Court dismissed the son’s appeal, ruling that the property had been transferred to him solely to facilitate a bank loan, not with the intention of transferring its beneficial ownership.

title: Strongest earthquake in nearly 150 years hits off Cuba, shakes Mexico, Florida
byline: A historically strong earthquake struck off Cuba’s northwest coast on Monday, according to official reports, shaking parts of Cuba, Mexico and ​Florida that are typically not prone to quakes.

title: Iconic actress Iranganie Serasinghe celebrates 99th birthday
byline: Beloved and iconic artiste Iranganie Serasinghe will celebrate her 99th birthday today. She was born in 1927. She has been a pioneering figure in Sri Lankan cinema. She has earned widespread admiration for her remarkable contribution to the country’s arts and cultural landscape.

title: US adds BYD to list of firms with alleged Chinese military ties
byline: The US has added several major firms from China including technology giant Alibaba and electric car maker BYD to a list of companies said to have ties with the Chinese military.

title: People lean heavily on personal loans for survival: Study
byline: Sri Lankans have increasingly turned to personal and consumption-related borrowing over the past two years, with personal loans recording a sharp 35 per cent increase between December 2024 and March 2026, the latest data show.

title: Trump says US will declare ‘total victory’ over Iran within two weeks
byline: US President Donald Trump announced Monday that the United States will declare “total victory” over Iran in the next two weeks, just hours after Tehran and Israel agreed to halt their latest escalation, Qazinform News Agency cites Anadolu Agency.

title: CID officers summoned by HRCSL over Suresh Sallay investigation
byline: The Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) has directed officers from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to appear before the commission this week to provide clarifications regarding the ongoing investigation into the former head of the State Intelligence Service (SIS), Suresh Sallay.

title: Key player misses out as West Indies name squad for Sri Lanka
byline: The West Indies have named a 15-player squad for their upcoming three-game T20I series at home against Sri Lanka.

title: Two killed in train-three-wheeler collision near Kadana
byline: Two people were killed when a three-wheeler collided with the Muthukumari Express train near the Kadana railway station this morning.

title: Somali referee Artan barred from entering USA
byline: Artan, the 2025 Confederation of African Football (CAF) men’s referee of the year, was barred from entering the country at Miami International Airport and is currently in Turkey.

title: Rain hands Sri Lanka 1-0 ODI series win over West Indies
byline: The third and final One-Day International (ODI) between West Indies cricket team and Sri Lanka national cricket team was abandoned without a ball being bowled on Monday after persistent rain rendered the outfield unplayable, handing Sri Lanka a 1-0 series victory.

title: Iran and Israel say they will pause strikes but warn of retaliation if ceasefire breached again
byline: Iran and Israel say they have halted attacks on each other, after the two countries exchanged fire for the first time since April’s truce.

title: Three die after restaurant fire near Thalawathugoda Junction
byline: All three victims who were injured following a fire at a restaurant near Thalawathugoda Junction have succumbed to their injuries, Police said.

title: Two fined Rs. 180,000 for killing protected barking deer
byline: A Nanu Oya court has imposed fines totaling Rs. 180,000 on two men arrested for killing and butchering a barking deer, a strictly protected species under Sri Lanka’s wildlife laws.

title: LIVE: Sri Lanka A vs India A, 1st Match at Dambulla
byline: India suffered an early setback in their chase as teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi departed for 14 off 12 balls, falling to a sharp catch at mid-off off the bowling of Shiraz. Looking to continue his aggressive start, Sooryavanshi attempted to hit through the line but failed to find the necessary elevation, handing Arachchige a comfortable catch. The wicket sparked jubilant celebrations from Shiraz and provided a crucial breakthrough for Sr

title: Sri Lanka sets 13% industrial emission cut as key step toward carbon neutrality by 2050
byline: Noting that the government has taken a landmark policy decision to double its emission reduction target for the industrial sector to a 13% commitment, authorities say this move forms the bedrock of Sri Lanka’s long-term climate strategy aimed at achieving 70% renewable energy generation by 2030 and complete carbon neutrality by 2050.

title: Ravi K questions Govt on IMF programme outcomes, future plans
byline: Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake today sought clarification from the Government on the outcomes of Sri Lanka’s International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme and the country’s economic strategy beyond the current arrangement.

title: Central Bank records Rs. 332.38 buy, Rs. 342.08 sell
byline: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka has issued the daily exchange rates for today (09), recording the buying price of the US dollar at Rs. 332.3805.

title: Sri Lankan workers to gain expanded job opportunities in Cyprus; social security issue to be resolved urgently
byline: Sri Lankan workers are set to receive expanded employment opportunities in Cyprus, while authorities have also moved to address long-standing concerns over social security benefits for retired migrant workers.

title: Trump says pilots safe after US Army Apache goes down near Hormuz
byline: U.S. President Donald Trump said early on Tuesday that ​the pilots of a U.S. Army ‌Apache helicopter that went down near the Strait of Hormuz ’’are fine.’’

title: Australia and Sri Lanka launch third phase of Operation Disi Rela
byline: Australia and Sri Lanka have reaffirmed their steadfast commitment to combating maritime crime with the launch of the third phase of ’Operation Disi Rela’, a joint maritime security initiative aimed at safeguarding regional waters from a range of evolving maritime threats. The operation was ceremonially inaugurated on 8 June 2026 at the Kingsbury Hotel in Colombo.

title: Social media used to target youth with prohibited tobacco products
byline: Social media platforms are being used to market prohibited tobacco products, including vapes and e-cigarettes, to young people in Sri Lanka, according to the Centre for Combating Tobacco.

title: Four injured in restaurant fire near Thalawathugoda Junction
byline: Four people were injured after a fire broke out at a restaurant near Thalawathugoda Junction, Police said.

title: Two clauses of Money Laundering Amendment Bill inconsistent with Constitution: Speaker
byline: The Supreme Court held that certain sections of Clauses 17 and 18 of the Money Laundering Amendment Bill are inconsistent with the Constitution and could be approved by a special majority (two thirds majority), Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne announced in Parliament today.

title: Ma Oya bridge closed today for debris removal; Use alternate routes
byline: (RDA) has announced that the Ma Oya Bridge will be closed to all vehicle traffic from 8.00 a.m. to 5.00 p.m. today (9) to facilitate debris removal operations following the impact of Cyclone Ditwa.

title: Sarana Gunawardena sentenced to four years imprisonment in corruption case
byline: Former Deputy Minister Sarana Gunawardena was today sentenced to four years of rigorous imprisonment by Colombo High Court judge Mohomed Mihal after being found guilty on corruption charges.

title: Sallay legally detained under provisions of PTA: Deputy Minister
byline: In the wake of various criticisms behind the detention of retired Major General Suresh Sallay, the former head of the State Intelligence Service, under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), Deputy Minister of Public Security Sunil Watagala said yesterday he was legally detained under provisions of the PTA and that there is nothing wrong with that.

title: Stop harassment of Suresh Sallay: Free Lawyers Association
byline: Free Lawyers Association yesterday urged the authorities to provide necessary medical treatment to former State Intelligence Service (SIS) Chief and amend laws which pave the way for the harassment of Sallay and others who are held under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA).

title: Apple unveils Siri AI makeover as Tim Cook bids farewell
byline: Apple has announced a significant overhaul of its digital assistant, unveiling Siri AI, which the company promised would offer a better artificial intelligence experience for users.

title: Mother wins three-decade legal battle over property against son
byline: A mother has emerged victorious in a 30-year legal battle against her son over a residential property after the Supreme Court dismissed the son’s appeal, ruling that the property had been transferred to him solely to facilitate a bank loan, not with the intention of transferring its beneficial ownership.

title: Strongest earthquake in nearly 150 years hits off Cuba, shakes Mexico, Florida
byline: A historically strong earthquake struck off Cuba’s northwest coast on Monday, according to official reports, shaking parts of Cuba, Mexico and ​Florida that are typically not prone to quakes.

title: Sri Lankans borrow more for survival
byline: Sri Lankans have increasingly turned to personal and consumption-related borrowing over the past two years, with personal loans recording a sharp 35 per cent increase between December 2024 and March 2026, the latest data show.

title: Sri Lanka emerging as a new base for Asia’s scam networks
byline: The crackdown on scam compounds in Cambodia is leading some gangs to relocate to beach resorts and office buildings in Sri Lanka, in what may be the next phase of one of the world’s fastest-growing criminal industries.

title: Trump says US in ‘final throes’ of Iran deal, Hormuz strait to open in days
byline: United States President Donald Trump has said that a deal between Israel and Iran is imminent, and that the two will leave each other alone for at least a week.

title: Red warning issued for fishermen as strong winds lash sea areas
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued an urgent Red Warning for the maritime and fishing community, warning that wind speeds could increase up to 70 kmph in sea areas off the coast from Kankesanthurai to Kalpitiya via Mannar.

title: Cabinet approves drafting of Digital Economy Bill
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to draft a Digital Economy Bill aimed at accelerating Sri Lanka’s digital transformation and promoting growth in the digital economy.

title: Sarana Gunawardena sentenced to 16 years of rigorous imprisonment
byline: Former Deputy Minister Sarana Gunawardena, who was found guilty in four corruption cases, was sentenced by Colombo High Court Judge Mohomed Mihal to four years’ imprisonment on each count.

title: Government to introduce demerit system for traffic offenses in September: Bimal
byline: The government is planning to introduce a demerit system for traffic offenses in September as a pilot project across the country, Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development Bimal Rathnayake said today.

title: Government railway season tickets go digital from July
byline: The issuance of concessionary railway season tickets for government officials will be fully digitized from July, allowing eligible public sector employees to obtain their tickets online through the Pravesha platform.

title: Over 200 stakeholders trained to put Sri Lanka’s Green Finance Taxonomy into practice
byline: More than 200 representatives from Sri Lanka’s financial sector, corporate institutions and public agencies have been trained on the practical implementation of the country’s Green Finance Taxonomy under a European Union-backed initiative aimed at accelerating sustainable investments.

title: Hayleys obtains enjoining order against Wimal Weerawansa
byline: The District Court of Kaduwela has issued an enjoining order against former MP Wimal Weerawansa on an application filed by Hayleys PLC over an alleged defamatory statement.

title: Train services likely to be disrupted amid planned trade union action
byline: Railway services are expected to face major disruption tomorrow due to planned trade union action by railway controllers, the Sri Lanka Railway Controllers’ Union (SLRCU) said.

title: CSE rebounds as lower oil prices and strong crossings lift sentiment
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) recovered from the previous session’s losses on Tuesday, with both benchmark indices closing higher as improving external factors helped restore investor confidence. The rebound was largely driven by a sharp decline in global oil prices and a modest appreciation of the Sri Lankan Rupee against the US Dollar, easing concerns over the potential economic fallout from the ongoing Middle East conflict.

title: 14-hour water cut in Galle tomorrow
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced a 14-hour water cut in the Galle Municipal Council area tomorrow (10) to facilitate essential maintenance work.

title: Dr. Satyanjal Pandey pays farewell call on Defence Secretary
byline: The outgoing Indian Deputy High Commissioner to Sri Lanka, Dr. Satyanjal Pandey, paid a farewell call on Sri Lanka’s Defence Secretary, Air Vice Marshal Sampath Thuyacontha, at the Ministry of Defence today.

title: Tickets for Iran fans revoked, says federation
byline: The World Cup, co-hosted by Canada, Mexico and the United States, begins on Thursday, with Iran scheduled to play New Zealand on 15 June and Belgium on 21 June - both in Los Angeles - before facing Egypt in Seattle on 26 June.

title: Lord’s pitch gets sanctioned by ICC
byline: The Lord’s and the Gaddafi stadium pitches where England took on New Zealand and Australia faced Pakistan in a Test and ODI respectively were rated as unsatisfactory by the ICC under the Pitch and Outfield Monitoring Process.

title: Dengue surge as thousands of breeding sites found in major national inspection drive
byline: A nationwide dengue control operation has revealed a worrying number of mosquito breeding sites, raising concerns over public health safety in key institutions including schools, government offices, and construction sites.

title: Principals’ starting salaries revised; Promotion relief granted
byline: The starting salary of officers in the Sri Lanka Principals’ Service has been revised following Cabinet approval, the Ministry of Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education announced.

title: Extension of emergency approved by Parliament
byline: The extension of the state of emergency for another month was approved by a majority of 128 votes.

title: Lanka Sathosa to reduce prices of 18 essential food items from tomorrow
byline: Lanka Sathosa has announced a reduction in the prices of 18 essential food items with effect from tomorrow (10), as part of a government initiative aimed at providing relief to consumers amid rising global prices.

title: 10-hour water cut in several Kalutara areas tomorrow
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) announced that water supply will be suspended for 10 hours in several areas of the Kalutara District tomorrow (10), due to an interruption in electricity supply to the Kehena Water Treatment Plant.

title: Permanent appointments for temporary staff recruited since 2018
byline: The Government yesterday formally granted permanent appointments to a group of employees recruited on temporary, casual, substitute, contract and concessionary basis under the Ministry of Trade, Commerce, Food Security and Cooperative Development.

title: One-third of schools inspected flagged for dengue risk
byline: Schools have emerged as one of the key areas of concern in an islandwide dengue eradication drive, with inspectors discovering mosquito breeding sites and larvae in several educational institutions.

title: Govt steps up preparations for possible El Niño impact
byline: The Government has begun preparing for the potential impacts of the anticipated global El Niño phenomenon, with special attention being paid to safeguarding food security, agriculture and water resources.

title: Carry out investigations, but don’t turn them political – Namal
byline: Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna National Organizer and Parliamentarian Namal Rajapaksa said that investigations into matters relating to national security and the Easter attacks must be conducted properly, but should not be politicized for political advantage.

title: EU plans to ban Russian soldiers from bloc in fresh sanctions on Moscow
byline: The EU hopes to ban Russian soldiers from entering its territory as part of further sanctions against Moscow that also target banks, crypto firms and the Kremlin’s oil revenues.

title: ‘Corruption led to economic collapse’ - Court
byline: While delivering the judgment, the High Court Judge underscored the far-reaching consequences of corruption in State institutions, observing that such misconduct not only damages the country’s economy but has also contributed to its economic downfall.
